source_description: From October 30-31, 2005, Rosa Parks lay in honor in the Capitol Rotunda. Parks was the first woman to lay in honor in the Capitol Rotunda and the second African-American. ... Authority for use of the Rotunda granted by Senate Concurrent Resolution 61, 109th Congress, 1st Session, agreed to October 29, 2005.
caption: Members of the public file past the casket of Rosa Parks, the civil rights pioneer, as she lies in honor in the Rotunda of the U.S. Capitol, Washington, D.C., October 2005. Photograph: Architect of the Capitol.
why_it_fits: A documentary photograph in which the Capitol Rotunda (its pilasters, historical paintings and statues) appears as the place where a named public event happened. The subject is the public filing past the casket; no partisan figure is the subject.
notes: The Architect of the Capitol mark sits at the lower right; crop it. Uniformed U.S. Capitol Police officers stand in the line of mourners.
